subject: Astronomy & Space
title: What Are Cosmic Rays?
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on What Are Cosmic Rays?.

hook.text: Cosmic rays are high-energy particles from space that constantly bombard Earth. Most are protons moving near light speed.

buildup.text: They come from the Sun, exploding stars, and mysterious sources beyond our galaxy. Their energies span a huge range.

discovery.text: Victor Hess discovered them in 1912 by carrying instruments in a balloon. Radiation increased with altitude—it came from space.

twist.text: Earth's atmosphere and magnetic field shield us. On Mars or in deep space, cosmic rays pose a serious risk to astronauts.

climax.text: The highest-energy cosmic rays carry as much energy as a baseball pitch—packed into a single subatomic particle.

punchline.text: Particles from exploding stars hitting us constantly. Our atmosphere keeps us safe.

quiz.question: How were cosmic rays first discovered?
options: Victor Hess found that radiation increased with altitude during balloon flights in 1912
They were detected by the first radio telescopes in the 1930s
Astronauts on the International Space Station measured them directly

details.summary: Cosmic rays are high-energy particles — mostly protons and atomic nuclei — that travel through space at nearly the speed of light. They originate from supernovae, active galactic nuclei, and other violent cosmic events.
details.whyItMatters: Cosmic rays constantly bombard Earth and influence atmospheric chemistry, cloud formation, and even biological mutation rates. They also serve as messengers from the most energetic processes in the universe.
takeaways: High-energy particles traveling near the speed of light
Originate from supernovae and active galactic nuclei
Create particle cascades when hitting Earth's atmosphere

faq.question: Are cosmic rays dangerous to astronauts?
faq.answer: Yes — they are a major health concern for long-duration space missions. Outside Earth's magnetic field, astronauts receive significantly higher radiation doses. Heavy cosmic ray nuclei can damage DNA and increase cancer risk. Shielding solutions for Mars missions remain an active area of research.

faq.question: Where do the highest-energy cosmic rays come from?
faq.answer: The highest-energy cosmic rays (ultra-high-energy cosmic rays) carry more energy than a tennis ball serve packed into a single proton. Their sources are debated — candidates include active galactic nuclei, gamma-ray bursts, and starburst galaxies.
